standard_prerequisites.name: A projective module is a direct summand of a free module
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Elementary standard fact used at proof lines 6659-6661, where a projective C with M direct sum C free is chosen; the counted proof cites no label
standard_prerequisites.use: Allows the surjection u to be replaced by u direct sum the identity on C, so that M may be assumed free, which is the first reduction of the proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Right exactness of the tensor product and the kernel of a base changed surjection
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Elementary standard fact used at proof lines 6666-6668; the counted proof cites no label
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies Ker(u tensor 1) with the image of Ker(u) tensor_A B, which is precisely what makes the condition that the coefficients of Ker(u) vanish equivalent to u tensor 1 being injective.

core_obligations: Reduce to M free: since M is projective there is a projective C with F = M direct sum C free, and replacing u by u direct sum 1 : F -> N direct sum C preserves both surjectivity and the equivalence to be proved (proof lines 6658-6662).

Define the ideal I of A generated by the coefficients, with respect to a fixed basis of the free module M, of all elements of the kernel of u, and show the equivalence: because u is surjective and tensoring with B is right exact, the kernel of u tensor 1 is the image of the kernel of u tensored with B, so u tensor 1 is injective exactly when every coefficient in I dies in B, i.e. exactly when the image of I under the ring map is zero (proof lines 6662-6668).
proof_roadmap: Use projectivity to make the source module free (proof lines 6658-6662).
Write down the ideal generated by the coefficients of the kernel and identify the kernel of the base changed map with the image of the kernel tensored with the test algebra (proof lines 6662-6668).
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, for a surjection u : M -> N of A-modules with M projective, an ideal I of A such that for every ring map A -> B the map u tensor 1 is an isomorphism exactly when I is mapped to zero in B (statement lines 6645-6656, tag 05PE). The proof is short but it is a real construction: projectivity is used to replace M by a free module without changing the question, and then the ideal is built from the coefficients of all elements of the kernel with respect to a basis, the equivalence following from the identification of the kernel of the base changed map with the image of the kernel after tensoring. The choice of ideal is the substance, so the claim is H2.
